claims.statement: At Danebury, grain was kept in storage buildings and sealed pits.
Danebury’s farming community kept sheep and cattle.
Evidence at Danebury includes cereal processing, weaving, leatherworking and metalworking.
Danebury obtained materials including metals and salt through exchange with other areas.
Four rectangular structures at Danebury have been interpreted as shrines.
Published accounts differ: Ford and Saunders use 550–100 BCE for Danebury, while Büster dates its construction around 470 BCE.
The Danebury map marker uses the Atlas of Hillforts site reference.

start.original: Published construction chronologies: 550 or around 470 BCE
